weighing.summary: Union commanders on the field give three kinds of figure. Buford, for his division, reports over 500 prisoners (Aug 29) and Gamble, for one of his brigades, about 511 of whom 61 went to Kilpatrick by mistake (Aug 24). Kilpatrick reports upward of 1,500 (second scan) or 1,600 (first scan) (Aug 7). Meade telegraphed on the day a brigade 1,500 strong, then 500 more, then over 2,000. Lee (Jul 21) and Heth (Sep 13) say no organized body was taken, only stragglers, and give no total. Other units report 50 to 400 each. Nothing in the record separates these: the commanders who were present disagree by a factor of three, the Confederates give no count, and the headquarters figures repeat Kilpatrick's claim. The conflict is irreducible; the default is the range from the lowest count of a division commander (over 500) to the highest dispatch of the day (over 2,000), and every figure stays selectable.
weighing.who: Buford commanded the First Division and Gamble its First Brigade; both were at the fight. Kilpatrick commanded the Third Division and led the charge on the hill. Meade was at army headquarters and wrote from reports. Lee wrote from the army's side and did not count. Heth commanded the rear guard and was engaged; he rejects the brigade claim and thinks most of the men lost on 14 Jul were taken on the road, before his engagement. Kidd (wounded early), Oates and McClellan wrote later and repeat the claims.
weighing.when: Meade's wires and the newspaper of 16 Jul are of the day (rank 6 and 4); Lee's letter is 7 days later; Kilpatrick, Gamble and Buford wrote 24 to 46 days later (official reports, ranks 5 and 4); Heth wrote two months later. The memoirs and histories are 1885 to 1935. By the owner's rule a dispatch of the day outranks a report of weeks and that a memoir; but the dispatches are relayed claims of one source (Kilpatrick), which Lee and Heth deny in kind, so the rank does not decide the count.
weighing.where: Buford, Gamble and Kilpatrick were present; the Union claims are for the whole day (Williamsport to the river), the division counts for what each command took in the fight near the ford. The two kinds may count different sets: the 1,500 of Kilpatrick and Meade is a brigade as a unit, the 500 of Buford is a count of men. Heth thinks that 3 out of 4 of the men the enemy took on 14 Jul were taken between Hagerstown and the point where he engaged, which would fit a day total larger than the count at the ford; he does not give a number.
weighing.how_knew: Buford, Gamble and Kilpatrick counted or were told by their own men; Meade relayed; the newspaper relayed officers. Lee says the number is not known to him; Heth gives "several hundred" from his own staff's work. No return of Confederate prisoners lost on 14 Jul was found. The partial counts (McKeen about 50; Williams 200-300; the 7th Michigan 400) are single commands and are not summed. Which digit Kilpatrick's report prints (1,500 or 1,600) is not settled: the two scans differ and the page image could not be fetched.
weighing.clock: not applicable: these are counts. The dispatches carry the Union headquarters' clock (3 p.m., 8:30 p.m., 9 p.m.); the 20-minute difference between the armies' clocks is not applied and does not matter to a count.
weighing.independence: Groups: (1) Buford and Gamble, one division (Buford wrote five days after Gamble; they are not counted as two witnesses); (2) Kilpatrick's claim, carried by Kilpatrick, Meade's dispatches (Heth names Kilpatrick as Meade's authority), the newspaper correspondent, Kidd, Custer's regimental summary and McClellan; (3) Lee and Heth, one Confederate denial; (4) McKeen; (5) Williams; (6) Oates and Freeman, no source stated. So the largest count rests on one claim; the lowest on one division. Each carries a single_source flag.

source_panel_text: Between over 500 and over 2,000 prisoners: Buford's report puts the capture by his division at over 500, Kilpatrick and Meade claimed 1,500 to over 2,000, and Lee and Heth deny any brigade was taken and give no count. The record is divided, so a range is shown. 6 other values are listed.

pdf_default.note: Over 500 is a documented count (Buford) and the low end of the range, but the Official Records also hold 1,500 to over 2,000 from Kilpatrick and Meade, so 500 alone is not the better-supported figure.

first_delegated.note: The two division counts (over 500; about 511) are right, but the first pass called 1,000-2,000 "secondary only": the Official Records themselves carry Kilpatrick's 1,500 or 1,600 and Meade's over 2,000, so the larger values are documented claims.
